title: Staged modernization cutover under unmeasured dual-write and reconciliation inputs
question: Should a staged modernization cutover proceed when dual-write lag and reconciliation capacity are assumed rather than measured?
context: A three-stage traffic shift is compared with a no-cutover baseline. The staged model uses an assumed dual-write lag and reconciliation capacity drawn from wide uniform ranges with a negative correlation. The baseline retains legacy traffic. Both models are synthetic; neither represents a performed migration or measured data quality.

constraints.statement: A cutover must not proceed without a measured dual-write lag and reconciliation capacity for the target environment.
A rollback must complete within the declared observation window before cutover is approved.
Business continuity ownership and a reconciliation runbook must be confirmed outside the simulation.

candidates.title: Staged traffic shift with rollback trigger
Retain legacy with no traffic shift

outcome.rationale: The staged candidate does not produce a decision-supported cutover. Its synthetic maximum divergence is 10,102.8 records (95% CI 7,670.7-12,534.9), and rollback does not complete within the 2,400-second horizon in any replication (rollback_completed 0.0). The no-cutover baseline has zero modeled divergence and no rollback requirement. Because the dual-write lag and reconciliation capacity are assumed over wide ranges and were not measured, the difference between the candidates cannot be attributed to a real migration path. The correct outcome is insufficient evidence, not a recommendation to cut over or to reject modernization permanently.
non_quantitative_constraints: M3 business continuity ownership is not established by the model.
No record-level reconciliation or schema compatibility was tested.

reversal_triggers: A measured dual-write lag with a bounded upper confidence limit and a measured reconciliation capacity in the target environment.
A rehearsed rollback that completes within the declared observation window and leaves no unexplained divergence.
A measured divergence below the declared business threshold across a sustained shadow or parallel-run period.
A changed stage schedule or target capacity that materially alters the reconciliation backlog.
Completion of the M3 continuity and reconciliation-runbook review.
limitations: The staged and baseline scenarios use synthetic inputs; no migration was performed.
Dual-write lag and reconciliation capacity are drawn from assumed ranges, not measurements.
The model does not represent record-level reconciliation, schema compatibility or deployment failures.
The divergence metric is a synthetic proxy and cannot be read as a data-quality measurement.
